Current source rejects lapsed covering evidence but permits acts without covering evidence; no runtime proof claimed.

# Radiator makes agent work visible and steerable across every team

> [!tldr]
> - Radiator is one workspace where teams and their agents plan, run, and review work across every department.
> - It records everything in an append-only event log, and checks that whoever holds control of agent work can still act on it.
> - Load this note at the start of every thread. Load a reference section only when the task needs it.

## How to use this brief

This note is the canon.
It is short on purpose, so it fits in any context alongside real work.
Each section ends with a link to the reference note that holds the detail.
Every statement in the brief carries a status: **Decided**, **Proposed**, or **Open**.
Treat Proposed and Open statements as questions, not instructions.
When a reader, human or agent, misreads the brief, add the question to [calibration-questions](calibration-questions.md) and fix the gap here or in the reference note.

## What Radiator is

**Decided.**
Radiator is an orchestration platform for work shared by people and AI agents.
Teams use it to shape work together, run it with agents, and see what happened.
The product promise is: automated work you can see, shape, and steer.
The through line is: you can't steer what you can't see.

The name comes from an information radiator: a display that makes the state of work visible to everyone who passes it.
The append-only event log is the radiator itself.

Radiator is built for every department, not only engineering.
Engineering is one team among about ten.

→ [01-vision-and-positioning](01-vision-and-positioning.md)

## What Radiator is not

**Decided.**

| Radiator is not | Because |
|---|---|
| A software factory for engineering only | Every team's work runs on the same model |
| A replacement for customers' trackers, wikis, or chat tools | We integrate where work is recorded, build where it is understood, and hold the record only when nobody else does |
| A governance layer bolted onto other vendors' agents | Governance is part of how Radiator runs work, not a separate product |
| A chat assistant | A chat session ends; Radiator keeps the work model, the team, and the record |
| Self-authorizing | No agent changes its own permissions or goals |

## The invariants

**Decided.**
These hold in every workspace and cannot be configured away.

1. The event log is append-only. Corrections are new events.
2. Every action names a principal and a responsibility.
3. Accountability traces to a person or role, even when a judge agent holds the conn.
4. Changing permissions, rules, or goals is its own decision, made by whoever the record allows.
5. When the evidence behind a control lapses, the actions that depend on it narrow or pause.

## The core vocabulary

**Decided.**
Use these terms exactly.
Do not rename them for variety.
The full list, with registers, is in [glossary](glossary.md).

| Term | Is | Is not |
|---|---|---|
| Responsibility | What a named person or role answers for. The primary unit. | A task, or a classification of work |
| Work item | An undertaking with completion criteria: a deal, a feature, an incident | A fixed sequence or duration |
| Lifecycle | The phases of a named work item, including rework. Always "lifecycle of what." | All the activity in a department |
| Round | One pass of recurring work, such as this month's close | A feedback loop, unless stated |
| Condition | Something kept within bounds (maintained) or retained untouched (dormant) | A position in a process |
| Trigger | What starts work: a commitment, schedule, event, or threshold | A kind of work |
| Rule or window | A constraint on other work, with its own start, expiry, and exceptions | A fourth shape of work |
| Loop | Agent-scale mechanics only: run loops, retries, validation loops | Organizational recurrence |
| The conn | Practical control of a piece of work: who can see, decide, and act on it now | A name in a field |
| Principal | Any actor with identity: a person, an agent, or an external system | A user account only |
| Gathering | A structured meeting or workshop with an agent facilitating: a standup, a retro, story mapping | A thread (an agent chat) or a round |
| Archetype | A reusable work pattern, such as approval and exception | A team-specific template |
| Workspace | The layer holding a team's configuration, access, and source bindings | A filter, or necessarily one org-chart team |
| Method pack | A team's way of planning, bundled as an extension | A change to the rules of control |

## The work model in one paragraph

**Decided.**
A trigger starts work inside a responsibility.
People and agents produce a work item through its lifecycle.
Rounds iterate on it: agents draft, people decide.
When a round runs the same way each time, it can be promoted to an automation.
A condition watched afterward raises a new trigger when it drifts.
Shape, dependencies, authority, and capability are designed together.
Neither "shape first" nor "allocation first" is the rule.
Work items nest through "part of," and every work item has checkable completion criteria.
Radiator is opinionated about meaning and neutral about method: a team's way of planning arrives as a method pack.

→ [02-the-work-model](02-the-work-model.md)

## Teams, workspaces, and tools

**Decided.**
A workspace is the layer that holds a team's configuration and access: its vocabulary, method pack, dial defaults, deciders, and the systems its work lives in.
Systems of record bind to workspaces, not to the organization; a workspace with no system uses Radiator's native record.
A work item has one home workspace, can be linked into others through "part of," and is visible to anyone named on its responsibility record.
A person's home view spans every workspace they belong to or are named in.

→ [02-the-work-model](02-the-work-model.md) · [05-integrations](05-integrations.md)

## How control works

**Decided.**
Each responsibility records five roles: accountable, decides, executes, may change the arrangement, and owed an account.
Control is current evidence, not a name in a box.
Evidence lists the acts it covers, the conditions under which it stays valid, and when it lapses.
Customers choose their stakes: the conn can sit with a person or with a judge agent.
Automation is a dial with five settings: manual, assisted, supervised, delegated, autonomous.

→ [03-governance-and-the-conn](03-governance-and-the-conn.md)

## How the system is built

**Decided.**
Radiator uses hexagonal architecture.
The core holds the work model, policy, and the event contract, with no vendor code.
Surfaces drive work in; adapters reach external systems; both meet the core through ports.
Governance is decided in the core, enforced at every port, and verified from the log.
Anything we build for customers, we build the way a customer could: as an extension on the same ports.

→ [04-architecture](04-architecture.md) · [05-integrations](05-integrations.md) · [06-surfaces](06-surfaces.md) · [08-extensibility](08-extensibility.md)

## How we talk about it

**Decided.**
Use three registers and keep them apart.

| Register | Where it lives | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Canonical | Code, events, prompts, this brief | responsibility, round, condition |
| Customer | The customer's own words, mirrored back | "the monthly close," "deal stages," "our agent factories" |
| Marketing | Public pages | "When agents do the work, who can still steer?" |

We build archetypes and market teams.
Gatherings bring teams in; archetypes keep them.

→ [07-archetypes-and-gatherings](07-archetypes-and-gatherings.md) · [09-go-to-market](09-go-to-market.md)

## Beyond Radiator

**Decided.**
Radiator is the workshop, not the storefront.
Some things are built in: extensions that run inside Radiator.
Others are built by: separate products Radiator builds and maintains, which run on their own and bind back as systems of record.
Spinoffs share edge libraries, never Radiator's core, and wait until the internal MVP and first pilot are done.
In public work, anyone can speak; only named people decide.

→ [11-built-in-and-built-by](11-built-in-and-built-by.md) · [12-blocks](12-blocks.md) · [13-public-gatherings](13-public-gatherings.md) · [14-beyond-software-companies](14-beyond-software-companies.md)

## Where we are

**Decided.**
Two engineers build Radiator today.
The MVP bar is that we use Radiator instead of other tools to build Radiator.
We act as forward-deployed engineers for our first customers, and field work ships only through extension points.

→ [10-organization-and-roadmap](10-organization-and-roadmap.md)

# The conn is control backed by current evidence, held by a person or a trusted judge agent

> [!tldr]
> - Every responsibility records five roles, and control over it must be backed by evidence that is still valid.
> - Customers choose their stakes: a person or a judge agent can hold the conn, but accountability always traces to a person or role.
> - Hard decisions get six resolution paths, and approvals that are only clicked through show up as nominal.

## The responsibility record

**Decided.**

| Role | Question |
|---|---|
| Accountable | Who answers for the outcome or obligation? |
| Decides | Who may make which decisions? |
| Executes | What may people and agents do? |
| Changes the arrangement | Who may revise permissions, rules, or goals? |
| Owed an account | Whose interests must be represented? (may be empty) |

Agents may execute and make bounded decisions.
Assigning them duties does not make them the accountable owner.

```yaml
# Illustrative
responsibility: payments-rollback
answers_for: payments available without losing valid transactions
accountable: role/payments-service-owner
decides:
  - who: role/incident-lead
    on: [rollback-with-data-risk]
executes:
  - who: agent/rollback
    may: [restart-replica, rollback-stateless]
    bounds:
      restart-replica: requires healthy_peer_replica
changes: role/platform-lead
owed_account: [finance-ops, affected-merchants]
evidence:
  - claim: incident-lead can judge data-loss risk
    basis: transaction-diff shown in approval view
    valid_while: [transaction-diff service reachable, incident-lead holds payments access]
    review: every 90 days
    on_lapse: require second approver from finance-ops
```

## Control evidence

**Decided.**
Three questions define practical control: who can notice trouble, who can act in time, and who answers for the consequences.
These can belong to different people and agents.

Evidence fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| claim | The capability asserted, scoped to named acts |
| basis | What supports it: a tool, a drill, a review, or labeled qualitative judgment |
| valid_while | Conditions that must keep holding |
| review | A maximum age, so evidence goes stale even when nothing visibly changes |
| on_lapse | What narrows, pauses, or escalates when the claim stops holding |

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  Verified --> Unverified: a valid_while fails or review age passes
  Unverified --> Verified: new evidence, logged with its basis
```

Example: an agent may restart a replica while another healthy replica carries traffic.
The other replica becomes unhealthy, so the bound fails.
Restart is suspended; separately authorized diagnosis continues.

## Stakes and judge agents

**Decided.**
Each organization chooses how much each step needs a person.
The conn can sit with a person or with a judge agent running a frontier model.
The same checks apply to either.
Accountability traces to whoever chose the arrangement.
Autonomy requires current authority, bounded consequences, and proportionate safeguards.
Reversibility is one safeguard, not a requirement.

## When a decision arrives

**Decided.**
The person or agent on record sees a decision card: the question, their role, a deadline with its escalation, links to evidence, and actions.

| Path | Effect |
|---|---|
| Decide | Approve, decline, or edit the proposal |
| Forward | Hand the call to someone better placed. The conn moves, with a relief briefing. |
| Tag people | Pull in voices where they already are. The conn stays. |
| Call | Start or schedule a decision call; the listening agent writes the outcome back |
| Chat about it | Ask the agent questions with full context loaded |
| Open on canvas | The operator preloads context and diagrams options |

Every path ends in one decision event, attributed to whoever made the call.

## Find the decider

**Decided.**
When nobody is clearly on record, an agent searches chats, email, call transcripts, tracker history, and responsibility records.
It names who can decide with authority and why, then offers to ask them where they already are.
This replaces the habit of defaulting to the product manager.

## Nominal approvals

**Decided.**
Fast approval is not a problem by itself.
A nominal approval is a mismatch: declared stakes are high and observed engagement is low.

| Signal | Use |
|---|---|
| Exposure: was the evidence opened? | Governance: conn status and audits |
| Patterns: always approves, never edits, approves in bursts | Governance |
| Outcomes: approvals later reverted or tied to incidents | Governance |
| Speed relative to size and risk | Private to the person |
| A background judge agent's view | Private to the person |
| Workload at the time | Private to the person |

Responses, in order: friction scaled to risk in the moment; a private offer to delegate or change what reaches the person; a suggested memory for the agent ("Dana skims copy changes; lead with the risky line"); conn status drops to unverified, and audits flag the step's design, not the person.

Guardrails: say what is measured, show people their own data first, no leaderboards, and weight exposure and outcomes over dwell time.
Workplace monitoring rules vary by country.

# Customers browse by team and start by running one real piece of their own work

> [!tldr]
> - Market teams, build archetypes. Archetype names never appear in customer copy.
> - A guided start on the customer's own work replaces a free trial, pending evidence.
> - Gatherings bring teams in with no setup; the work they produce pulls in integrations and automations.

## Navigation

**Decided.**
Five menu columns, in Factory's taxonomy with our changes:

| Column | Contents |
|---|---|
| Teams | Engineering, product and design, marketing, sales and success, finance, people, legal, IT and security |
| Workflows | Archetypes in customer words: intake and triage, drafts and reviews, approvals, recurring reviews, launches, calls to action items, audit evidence |
| Gatherings | Standups, retros, story mapping, research synthesis, design critiques, deal reviews, pre-mortems |
| Surfaces | Workspace, canvas, operator, calls, Dispatch, decisions |
| Platform and deployment | Event log, Conn, connectors, compute, models; managed and hybrid deployment |

Teams replaces Industries until a regulated customer proves the fit.
Private deployment comes later.

## Team pages

**Decided.**
Each team page has five parts:

1. A promise in the team's own words. Example for finance: "Close the books in days, and see only the exceptions."
2. Their work in our model: one round, one work item, one condition.
3. Four starter kits, each tagged with the workflow it is built on.
4. Where people decide, named by role.
5. The tools it connects to, and a guided start built on their own work.

The "built on" tags tell a buyer with several teams that one set of machinery serves all of them.
That is the cross-sell.
Starter kits can come as pairs: one gathering plus the automation it feeds.

## Getting started

**Proposed.**
A guided start, not a free trial.
The first session is with us, on the customer's own work.

| Step | What happens |
|---|---|
| Describe it | Talk to the operator or drop in a doc, ticket, or link |
| See its shape | Radiator drafts work items, rounds, and decision points on the canvas |
| Connect two tools | Only the ones this work touches |
| Run the first round | Agents draft; the customer decides |
| Promote what works | Turn the dial up when a round runs the same way twice |

## Land and expand

**Decided.**

1. **Land:** "Run your next retro in Radiator." No integrations, no setup, the whole team in the first hour.
2. **Connect:** action items need a home, so the team connects a tracker.
3. **Automate:** follow-through runs between gatherings.
4. **Expand:** invited guests from other teams see their own gatherings and starter kits.

## Jobs to be done

**Decided.**
Visitors can try Radiator by building something from their own job.

| Team | Job |
|---|---|
| Engineering | When we have a backlog of migrations, I want agents to work through them in parallel, so I only review what's risky. |
| Marketing | When we launch, I want brief to assets to published without chasing anyone, so I can focus on the message. |
| Sales | When a deal stalls, I want to know before the forecast call, so I can act while it still matters. |
| Finance and operations | When month-end comes, I want the close to run itself and show me only the exceptions. |

## Compared with a chat assistant

**Decided.**
"Great for a first draft. Radiator is where the work lives after."

| | A chat or vibe-coding session | Radiator |
|---|---|---|
| Memory | Ends with the session | A persistent work model the team shares |
| Who's involved | One person, one assistant | Teammates and many agents |
| Tools | Copy and paste | Connected to systems of record |
| Recurring work | Re-prompt every time | Rounds, triggers, automations |
| Scale | One thread | Dozens of runs, sorted by attention |
| Accountability | Whoever pasted the output | Responsibilities, decision points, the conn |
| History | Scrollback | A queryable, append-only record |

## Industries and compliance

**Decided.**
Regulated buyers fit our governance, but need trust material first: a trust center, service-level agreement, data processing agreement, and security page (NEED).
Financial services is the most natural first vertical.
